dedupe_keys.name: un habitat access to basic services in cities and urban areas water sanitation waste collection energy housing

description: This dataset gives the proportion of urban populations with access to basic services, compiled by UN-Habitat's Data and Analytics Section for its urban indicators database and published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. Indicators include improved water and sanitation, clean energy for lighting and cooking, internet and telephone connection, solid waste management services, durable housing and sufficient living area, reported for urban areas by country. Coverage is global, with observations from 1990 to 2023 depending on the country, and the file is refreshed yearly. Data are one Excel workbook, free under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License, with methods on UN-Habitat's data guidance pages. Caveats: values come from household surveys and censuses of different years, so countries are not strictly comparable; urban definitions are national; and waste collection access says nothing about how waste is treated. Simulation uses: setting service coverage baselines for urban waste collection and water models, identifying underserved urban populations for vulnerability analysis, and tracking SDG 11 progress. Related records: the UN-Habitat Waste Wise Cities Tool (platform-un-habitat-waste-wise-cities-tool) supports measuring collection coverage in cities, and Eurostat municipal waste statistics (data-eurostat-env-wasmun) give European treatment data.
